purpose: Reserve stable cross-Scope identifiers while keeping identity, authority and reusable Feature assignment separate.

system_id.authority_rule: Governed by the language-system identity registry and Current Governance.

scope_id.authority_rule: Created and governed by Current Scope governance; Scope identifiers are mutable in structure but stable while referenced.

era_id.authority_rule: Governed by the Current ERA registry inside its owning Scope.

work_id.authority_rule: Governed by the Scope in which the canonical work record originates.

media_id.authority_rule: Governed by the Scope containing the canonical media record; media Features do not own the asset.

event_id.authority_rule: Governed by the Scope containing the canonical event record.

fragment_id.authority_rule: Governed by the source Scope; governance/interpretation is a Feature projection unless explicitly canonicalized.

analysis_id.authority_rule: Governed by the source Scope; linguistic/retrieval analysis is a reusable Feature.

governance_id.authority_rule: Governed by Current Governance for the affected Scope.

rules: IDs are stable machine references and should not be renamed when display text changes.
Display names may change through their authority registry without changing linked IDs.
A record belongs to one governed Scope and may be consumed by multiple Features without transferring ownership.
Historical LOC1–8 identifiers may be retained only as explicit provenance/compatibility evidence.
A governance event may change lifecycle or interpretation without changing the stable identity of the historical source record.
Superseded records keep their stable IDs and point to replacement/successor IDs rather than being silently renumbered.
